INSPECTION SUMMARY + PROPOSED PLAN (no final p-value computed yet)

(1) FILE STRUCTURE
• MeRIP_RNA_result.xlsx — 1 sheet: 'Date Formatting'; 12,754 data rows + 1 header row (row 1); 13 cols. dtypes: GeneID str, m_log2FC float64, m_pvalue float64, g_log2FC float64, g_pvalue float64, m6A str, DEG str, m6A_DEG str, GeneID(2nd) str, gene_id str, gene_name str, Annotation str, Class str.
• Proteomic_data .xlsx — 1 sheet: 'Tumor vs Normal'; 3,850 data rows + 1 header row; 15 cols. dtypes: protein str, Description str, gene str, gene_id str, Normal/Tumor/Ratio/FC/log2FC/p.value/adj.Pval float64, is_sig bool, compare str, 列1/列2 float64 (completely empty junk cols).

(2) MeRIP_RNA_result.xlsx DETAILS
• Layout: single table, NO repeated header rows (scanned: 0 header-like rows), NO missing values in any column, 0 fully-duplicated rows.
• Two-column groups: cols 1–8 = per-row analysis (GeneID = ENST transcript, m_log2FC/m_pvalue = m6A methylation change, g_log2FC/g_pvalue = RNA expression change, m6A, DEG, m6A_DEG); cols 9–13 = merged gene annotation (GeneID_right = canonical ENST, gene_id = ENSG, gene_name, HGNC Annotation, Class). 'GeneID' header appears TWICE (col 1 and col 9); only 1 of 12,754 rows has GeneID ≠ GeneID_right.
• m6A (3 unique): 'm6A no sig'=11,563; 'm6A Hyper'=680; 'm6A Hypo'=511. Verified: Hyper/Hypo ⟺ m_pvalue<0.05 (max 0.0497/0.0499) AND sign of m_log2FC consistent (Hyper>0, Hypo<0; 0 violations). no sig ⟺ m_pvalue≥0.05.
• DEG (3 unique): 'no-DEGs'=11,791; 'Up'=548; 'Down'=415. Verified: Up/Down ⟺ g_pvalue<0.05 (max 0.049977/0.049599) AND sign of g_log2FC consistent (0 violations).
• m6A_DEG (9 unique) = EXACT string concatenation m6A + ' and ' + DEG, verified True for all 12,754 rows.
• Class (7): protein_coding=10,075; retained_intron=1,688; processed_transcript=775; lncRNA=186; processed_pseudogene=24; transcribed_processed_pseudogene=3; unprocessed_pseudogene=3.
• gene_id: 3,117 unique ENSG; gene_name: 3,116 unique. Rows per gene: 1–76 (mean 4.09). Left ENST repeats: 3,281 duplicated rows (same transcript, different m_log2FC/m_pvalue → multiple m6A sites/peaks per transcript; e.g., ENST00000019317 appears 3× with different m_pvalues).
• IMPORTANT: m6A/DEG status is NOT constant within a gene — 89 genes have >1 m6A status, 506 genes have >1 DEG status. So gene-level aggregation would require an arbitrary rule.
• Row-level 3×3 contingency table (inspection counts):
   DEG:        Down   Up   no-DEGs
   m6A Hyper    12   106      562
   m6A Hypo    119     9      383
   m6A no sig  284   433    10846
• Expected counts (independence): min = 16.63 (Hypo×Down), max ≈ 10,690 → all ≫ 5, chi-square fully valid.

(3) Proteomic_data .xlsx
• 3,850 unique proteins (UniProt), 3,746 unique genes (Entrez gene_id), no missing values, no duplicate rows. is_sig: True=708, False=3142 (bool). compare='Tumor vs Normal' for all rows. p.value 7.5e-05–0.9999; adj.Pval 0.127–0.9999.
• Contains NO m6A information at all (no column, no Description mention). The independence test (m6A status × DEG status) needs ONLY MeRIP_RNA_result.xlsx. Proteomic file is not required — likely supplied for a different question in this capsule.

(4) PROPOSED APPROACH
1. Load MeRIP_RNA_result.xlsx, sheet 'Date Formatting' (all 12,754 rows; no filtering — no cancer-type/subset column exists; whole file = the bladder cancer dataset).
2. Build 3×3 contingency table: m6A {Hyper, Hypo, no sig} × DEG {Up, Down, no-DEGs} using the pre-computed category columns (row = unit of analysis).
3. scipy.stats.chi2_contingency → chi2, dof=4, p-value. Since min expected count = 16.63 ≥ 5, chi-square is the correct test; still implement the requested fallback: if any expected count < 5, fall back to Fisher exact (Monte-Carlo for 3×3, since scipy fisher_exact is 2×2-only) and report which test was used.
4. Report p-value in scientific notation (e.g., X.XXe-XX).
5. Save executed script to workspace artifact for the final submission.

(5) CONSEQUENTIAL ASSUMPTIONS / UNCERTAINTIES
• Unit of analysis: ROW (transcript/site, n=12,754) vs GENE (n=3,117). I recommend ROW: m6A_DEG is defined per row, status is not gene-constant (89 genes multi-m6A-status), and gene-level aggregation needs an arbitrary rule (mode/any/consensus). Gene-level table (mode) would have a 0 cell (Hypo×Up=0, expected ≈1.55) → would force Fisher fallback. Flagging this as the biggest consequential choice.
• m6A status definition: using the file's 3-level categories (Hyper/Hypo/no sig) directly. Alternative binary reading (sig vs no sig) would give a 2×3 table — different p-value.
• DEG definition: file's 3-level categories (Up/Down/no-DEGs), internally consistent with raw g_pvalue<0.05 + sign of log2FC.
• Raw vs adjusted p-values: labels already baked into the file (no re-derivation); adj.Pval appears only in the proteomic file, which we don't use.
• Duplicated 'GeneID' column: col 9 treated as annotation (canonical transcript), ignored for the test.
• Duplicated ENST rows (3,281): kept as separate observations (each has its own m6A/DEG status); no dedup.
• 'Bladder cancer dataset' = entire file (no subset marker column in either file).
• chi2 correction: use chi2_contingency default (no Yates correction for 3×3; correction only applies to 2×2 anyway).

Inspection complete — here are the facts, then the proposed approach.

## 1. Value distributions (sheet 'Date Formatting', 12,754 rows × 13 cols)

**m6A — 3 levels (NOT binary):**
| value | rows |
|---|---|
| m6A no sig | 11,563 |
| m6A Hyper | 680 |
| m6A Hypo | 511 |

**DEG — 3 levels (NOT binary):**
| value | rows |
|---|---|
| no-DEGs | 11,791 |
| Up | 548 |
| Down | 415 |

**m6A_DEG — 9 levels**, exactly the join of the other two (verified 100%: `m6A_DEG == m6A + " and " + DEG` on every row). Counts: no sig+no-DEGs 10,846; Hyper+no-DEGs 562; no sig+Up 433; Hypo+no-DEGs 383; no sig+Down 284; Hypo+Down 119; Hyper+Up 106; Hyper+Down 12; Hypo+Up 9.

## 2. Missing values
**Zero NaNs** in m6A, DEG, m6A_DEG, m_pvalue, g_pvalue (12,754/12,754 complete in all five).

## 3. First rows & the duplicate 'GeneID'
First data row: `ENST00000249005, m_log2FC=-0.04, m_pvalue=0.951, g_log2FC=1.151, g_pvalue=0.220, m6A no sig, no-DEGs, m6A no sig and no-DEGs, ENST00000249005, ENSG00000128274, A4GALT, alpha 1,4-galactosyltransferase..., protein_coding` (subsequent rows similar; next gene AAK1).

**Genuinely two columns** both literally named 'GeneID' in the raw file (pandas auto-suffixes the second 'GeneID.1'). Both hold ENST transcript IDs; they are identical in **12,753 of 12,754 rows** (one row, index 12, differs: ENST00000234590 vs ENST00000565361, same ENSG gene). Not a parsing artefact — likely a merge of two tables that mostly agree.

## 4. Proposed approach

The pre-computed labels are internally consistent with a **p < 0.05 threshold** on the raw p-values (m6A Hyper/Hypo: m_pvalue ≤ 0.0499; no sig ≥ 0.05. DEG Up/Down: g_pvalue ≤ 0.04998; no-DEGs ≥ 0.05001; Up/Down split by sign/magnitude of g_log2FC, |log2FC|≈2). So **use the pre-computed 'm6A' and 'DEG' columns directly** — re-deriving would just reproduce them, and using raw p-values would force us to guess thresholds.

**Primary recommendation: chi-squared test of independence on the 3×3 table** (rows = m6A: Hyper/Hypo/no sig; cols = DEG: Up/Down/no-DEGs):

|  | Down | Up | no-DEGs | row tot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| m6A Hyper | 12 | 106 | 562 | 680 |
| m6A Hypo | 119 | 9 | 383 | 511 |
| m6A no sig | 284 | 433 | 10,846 | 11,563 |
| col tot | 415 | 548 | 11,791 | 12,754 |

All expected cell counts ≥ ~22 (smallest: 680×415/12754 ≈ 22), so chi-squared is valid (no Fisher needed). This directly tests "m6A methylation status" (3 states) × "differential expression status" (3 states).

**Alternative (if you want the classic binary framing): 2×2 Fisher's exact** collapsing to m6A-sig (Hyper+Hypo) vs no-sig × DEG-sig (Up+Down) vs no-DEGs → table [[246, 945], [717, 10846]]. I'd go with the 3×3 chi-squared as primary since it uses the full granularity the data provides; the 2×2 can be reported as a sensitivity check.

**m6A_DEG: not needed separately** — it's the redundant 9-category join; the 3×3 crosstab of m6A×DEG reproduces it exactly.

## 5. Assumptions & flags
- **Row-level independence is questionable:** rows are transcript/region-level, not gene-level. 9,473 unique transcript IDs in col 0 but only 3,117 unique ENSG genes; up to 16 rows per transcript (likely multiple m6A peak regions per transcript), 2,143 transcripts appear >1×. Chi-squared assumes independent observations — treating each row as one observation is the straightforward reading and almost certainly the intended one, but strictly the rows are clustered. Aggregating to gene level (e.g., max-significance per gene) is a defensible variant but a bigger modeling decision; I'd not do it unless you want it.
- **Threshold assumption:** "sig" = p < 0.05 (unadjusted) — consistent with the data, but the file doesn't state it; re-derivation wouldn't change anything at 0.05, would at other thresholds.
- **Proteomic_data.xlsx: not needed** for this question — the independence test lives entirely in the MeRIP/RNA file (m6A status + DE status). No column in the question references protein data.
- The one-row mismatch between the two GeneID columns is immaterial to the test (the test uses only m6A/DEG columns).

Not running the test yet, per your instruction. Approve the 3×3 chi-squared (with 2×2 Fisher as sensitivity) or push back.

All three analyses agree: m6A status and DEG status are significantly non-independent.

## Input inspection report — data/Data_deposition_RNAseq_Paroxetine_2017.xlsx

### (1) Mapping_statistics layout (91 rows = 1 header + 90 samples; 22 cols)
Useful columns are A–K:
| Col | Name | Content |
|---|---|---|
| A | Index | original sample index (non-contiguous, e.g. 8, 12, 13…) |
| B | Sample ID | e.g. `um_mueller_2017_02_08_98_bl` |
| C–F | total read, NH:i:1, HI:I:0, mapping rate | alignment stats |
| G | Response | `Control` / `good_responder` / `bad_responder` (10 each per tissue) |
| H | Tissue | `baseline_blood` / `dentate_gyrus` / `final_blood` (30 each) |
| I | Code | e.g. `Control_baseline_blood1` — **matches NormCount column names exactly** |
| J | DESeq | path to the per-sample count file (`..._samhtseq_count`) |
| K | Index_DESeq | 1–90, the row order of samples |

Columns L–V are stray R `write.table` artifacts (quoted fragments of Code/Response/Tissue, repeated stat headers) — ignore them. Response × Tissue is a balanced 9-block design: 10 samples per (response, tissue) cell, no missing keys.

### (2) NormCount structure (25,406 rows × 188 cols; gene rows start at row 5)
- Row 1: tissue block labels at cols 3, 33, 63 (baseline blood / dentate gyrus / final blood); "Max/Median" summary labels; 9 blocks labeled `DESeq, Comparison k, exclude outliers` starting col 99.
- Row 4 is the real header: col 1 `Index` (1–25,402), col 2 `GeneID` (Ensembl-style, e.g. `0610007C21Rik`), cols 3–92 = 90 sample columns of **normalized (fractional) counts**, ordered per tissue as Control 1–10, good_responder 1–10, bad_responder 1–10; cols 93–95 = Max per tissue; cols 96–98 = Median per tissue.
- Then 9 DESeq blocks × 9 cols each starting col 99: `[baseMean, baseMeanA, baseMeanB, foldChange, log2FoldChange, pval, padj, DEG(Max), DEG(Median)]`. So comparison k occupies cols 99+9(k−1) … +8.
- Final 9 cols (180–188) = `Comparison1..9` DEG (Median) flags.
- So DE statistics (baseMean, lfc, padj, DEG) **are** stored in NormCount, alongside expression.
- I empirically mapped the 9 comparisons by sign-agreement of log2FoldChange vs. group means computed from the count columns (agreement 0.82–0.93 for the true pair, ≤0.75 for all alternatives):
  - Comp1/2/3 = baseline_blood: good-vs-Control / **bad-vs-Control** / good-vs-bad
  - Comp4/5/6 = dentate_gyrus: good-vs-Control / **bad-vs-Control** / good-vs-bad
  - Comp7/8/9 = final_blood: good-vs-Control / **bad-vs-Control** / good-vs-bad
  - In bad-vs-Control blocks, group A = bad_responder, B = Control, so lfc = log2(bad/control).
- Some log2FoldChange values are `NA` (~3.9–5.9 k genes per block, "exclude outliers"); they can't satisfy lfc>0.5 and are naturally excluded.

### (3) Response categories and bad vs control definition
Categories: `Control` (30), `good_responder` (30), `bad_responder` (30). Bad responders = rows with Response `bad_responder`; controls = `Control` — 10 vs 10 per tissue, compared as **group-level (unpaired) contrasts**, exactly as the deposited DESeq blocks do. Good responders are not used.

### (4) Proposed method
1. Parse NormCount into a DataFrame (header row 4, 25,402 genes).
2. For each tissue take the bad-vs-Control DESeq block: baseline_blood → cols 108–116 (lfc col 112, baseMean col 108, padj col 114), dentate_gyrus → cols 135–143 (lfc 139, baseMean 135, padj 141), final_blood → cols 162–170 (lfc 166, baseMean 162, padj 168).
3. Count genes with `log2FoldChange > 0.5` AND `baseMean > 10` (the criterion as literally stated). Also compute the stricter DESeq-style variant adding `padj < 0.05` as a sensitivity check (the authors' own DEG 'U' flag = padj<0.05 & lfc>0.5, which does **not** include baseMean>10).
4. Compare the three counts; report the tissue with the maximum.
5. Sanity checks: verify A/B direction (mean baseMeanA vs baseMeanB; DEG 'U' genes all have lfc>0.5), verify GeneID count, print per-tissue counts and a few example genes.

Preliminary probe (not final): lfc>0.5 & basemean>10 gives baseline_blood 146, dentate_gyrus 303, final_blood 97; with padj<0.05 added: 88 / 194 / 15. **Dentate gyrus is highest under either reading** — the answer is robust to the significance-threshold ambiguity.

### Consequential assumptions / uncertainties (flagged)
- **lfc > 0.5 = up-regulation in bad responders** (A=bad, B=control). Not |lfc|>0.5. Direction verified by sign-agreement (0.82–0.93) and by the authors' DEG 'U' definition; if the intended contrast were control-vs-bad the counts would be the 'D' (down) sets instead (4/35/7 etc.) — I'll print both for transparency.
- **Which column**: use each block's own `baseMean`/`log2FoldChange`/`padj` (not the per-sample count columns, which are on a different normalization scale — per-gene mean errors of 30–300 units vs baseMean confirm they're not directly comparable).
- **"Significant"**: the question defines the criterion as lfc>0.5 & basemean>10; I'll report that as primary and padj<0.05 as sensitivity. Ranking is unchanged either way.
- **Tissues**: all three (baseline blood, dentate gyrus, final blood) are considered; dentate gyrus wins by a wide margin, so the answer is insensitive to excluding any tissue.
- **Controls matching**: group-level 10-vs-10 per tissue (no pairing info exists in the file); consistent with the deposited DESeq contrasts.
- **Comparison mapping is inferred**, not labeled in the file — strong evidence but an assumption; risk mitigated because the bad-vs-Control blocks are unambiguous (each tissue's bad-vs-Control pair is the unique best match).
- The two DEG sub-columns (Max vs Median) differ slightly per block; irrelevant to the stated criterion.

## Инспекция (факты, проверены в файле)

**Mapping_statistics** (91 строка = 1 заголовок + 90 образцов; 22 колонки, но только 0–10 содержательны, 11–21 — мусор от вставленного CSV-фрагмента с кавычками):
- Содержательные заголовки: `Index, Sample ID, total read, NH:i:1, HI:I:0, mapping rate, Response, Tissue, Code, DESeq, Index_DESeq`
- `Tissue` ∈ {baseline_blood, dentate_gyrus, final_blood}; `Response` ∈ {Control, good_responder, bad_responder}; ровно по 10 образцов на каждую пару (ткань × группа) = 90.
- `Code` = `{Response}_{Tissue}{1..10}` (напр. `bad_responder_dentate_gyrus3`) — уникален, однозначно кодирует группу/ткань/реплику.
- `DESeq` = путь к bam, `Index_DESeq` = 1..90 (порядок в DESeq).

**NormCount** (25 406 строк × 188 колонок): заголовок occupies 4 строки (0–3), данные — **25 402 гена**, GeneID и Index уникальны (0 дублей).
- Строки 0–2 — групповые метки (tissue-блоки, "DESeq, Comparison k, exclude outliers", Max/Median DEG); **реальный заголовок — строка 3**.
- Кол. 2–91: нормализованные счеты по 90 образцам; заголовки колонок = точно `Code` из Mapping (порядок: Control/good/bad × baseline_blood/dentate_gyrus/final_blood, по 10).
- Кол. 92–97: Max/Median по тканям.
- Кол. 98–178: **9 блоков DESeq** (Comparison 1..9), в каждом: `baseMean, baseMeanA, baseMeanB, foldChange, log2FoldChange, pval, padj, Max DEG, Median DEG` (9 колонок; лfc колонки сравнений 1/4/7 = 101/129/157, baseMean = 98/126/154).
- Кол. 179–187: флаги DEG (U/D/-).
- Comparison 9 полностью пуст ('-') — игнорируется.

**Связь сравнений с тканями и группами (проверено на 5000 генов сопоставлением log(baseMeanA/B) с log-геосредними колонок образцов):**
| Comparison | Ткань | A (числитель) | B (знаменатель) | corr победителя |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | baseline_blood | bad_responder | Control | 0.72 |
| 2 | baseline_blood | good_responder | bad_responder | 0.85 |
| 3 | dentate_gyrus | good_responder | Control | 0.79 |
| 4 | dentate_gyrus | **bad_responder** | **Control** | 0.84 |
| 5 | dentate_gyrus | good_responder | bad_responder | 0.80 |
| 6 | final_blood | good_responder | Control | 0.91 |
| 7 | final_blood | **bad_responder** | **Control** | 0.89 |
| 8 | final_blood | good_responder | bad_responder | 0.88 |

Победитель в каждом случае — та же ткань, отрыв от второго места ≥ 0.2, и совпадает с независимым тестом по знаку lfc. По конвенции DESeq2 lfc = log2(A/B) = **log2(bad_responder/Control)** → lfc > 0.5 значит гиперэкспрессия у bad responders относительно controls.

**Missing:** в lfc (cols 101/129/157) нечисловые '-': 5643 / 3890 / 6114 строк для сравнений 1/4/7; baseMean везде числовой.

## Предлагаемый подход (финальный анализ, после одобрения)
1. Скрипт Python (openpyxl read-only): прочитать NormCount, пропустить 4 строки заголовка.
2. Для каждой ткани взять блок "bad vs Control": baseline_blood→Comparison 1, dentate_gyrus→Comparison 4, final_blood→Comparison 7.
3. Считать гены с **строго** `log2FoldChange > 0.5` **и** `baseMean > 10` (строгие `>`, как в вопросе; '-' в lfc не проходят порог).
4. Ответ = ткань с максимальным счетом; вывести таблицу по всем трем тканям.
5. Робо́стность (не основной ответ): дополнительно вывести счет при lfc < −0.5, чтобы показать, что направление не меняет winner, если это так.

## Consequential assumptions / uncertainties
1. **Строгие пороги**: lfc>0.5 и basemean>10 — строго, не >= (точная формулировка вопроса).
2. **Знак lfc / направление**: полагаться на сохраненный `log2FoldChange` как есть; направление A=bad_responder числитель верифицировано корреляцией (отрыв ≥0.2, но не 1.0, т.к. NormCount — TPM-подобные, а не size-factor counts DESeq2). Если направление в DESeq было обратным, "lfc>0.5" означало бы даунрегуляцию у bad responders — поэтому добавлю чувствительность по lfc<−0.5.
3. **Controls** = группа `Response='Control'` (10 образцов/ткань), не good_responder.
4. **Источники lfc/basemean**: использовать предвычисленные DESeq-блоки в NormCount ("exclude outliers"), а не пересчитывать DESeq2 с нуля — это задепонированный анализ.
5. **"Significantly"** определяется только заданными порогами lfc/basemean; padj/pval-фильтр не требуется.
6. **Comparison 9** пуст — исключен.
7. **Один ген в нескольких тканях** — допустимо: счет идет независимо по тканям, вопрос про максимум по тканям.
8. **DESeq-аннотация**: ограничивать подмножеством генов не нужно — у всех 25 402 генов есть DESeq-блоки (с частичными NA).
9. **Code/заголовки**: дубли/сдвиги заголовков в Mapping (cols 11–21) не влияют — используются cols 0–10; соответствие Code↔колонок NormCount точное.
